sections.html:
Warren is the Trumbull County seat, on the Mahoning River about 14 miles northwest of Youngstown and 56 miles southeast of Cleveland. Selling here means dealing with a city whose rules for rentals, vacant houses and contractors are written into its Codified Ordinances. The population is an estimated 38,328, below the 39,201 counted in 2020 and the 41,557 counted in 2010.

The steps below cover the city and county offices a seller meets, starting with the numbers.

The city has low values and many renters.

  • Owners occupy 56.1% of housing units.
  • The middle owner-occupied house is valued at $86,400.
  • Owners pay $967 a month with a mortgage and $409 without one.
  • Gross rent at the midpoint is $766.
  • There are 16,871 households with 2.16 people each.
  • Household income at the midpoint is $37,887.

At these values a repair bill can equal a large share of the price. Buyers weigh condition closely and expect the seller to say what's wrong. Many older buildings from the late 19th and early 20th centuries still stand around Courthouse Square, and the mills that built the town are long gone, so expect aged systems in a lot of houses.

Under section 1367.10 of Warren's Codified Ordinances, no dwelling unit without at least one owner living in it can be occupied without a residential non-owner occupied dwelling permit from the Health Officer's office. The permit is issued after a Building Inspector confirms compliance with the Housing, Building, Zoning and fire codes.

  • The annual fee for a single-unit dwelling is $120, and multi-unit buildings pay $100 per unit for two to fifty units, with lower per-unit rates above that.
  • A permit lasts one year and can't be transferred to a new owner, so whoever buys a tenant-occupied house applies in their own name.
  • The Water Department won't open service for a non-owner-occupied unit without proof of the permit.
  • Occupying a unit without a permit carries a $1,000 fine, and each day counts as a separate violation.

Before listing a rental, ask the Health Department whether the permit is current, and tell the buyer it doesn't travel with the deed.

sections.h2: When an empty house counts as vacant
sections.html:
Chapter 1338 sets up a Vacant Property Registry. An owner has 30 days after a structure becomes vacant to register it with the Code Official. The annual fee is $200 for a residential structure, though it can be avoided if the property is secured, free of trash, mowed, and shows a visible address. Missing the filing deadline costs $50 per day up to $1,000.

One rule bears directly on a sale. A house under a signed broker listing agreement isn't counted as vacant during the first six months of that listing, while an empty house offered for sale by its owner counts as vacant immediately. If you've moved out and plan to sell without a broker, register or secure the property first.

sections.h2: Hiring a contractor before you sell
sections.html:
You don't always need one. Chapter 1305 makes contractors register with the city, posting a $25,000 surety bond and showing insurance, yet it exempts a homeowner working on the single-family house they live in. That owner files a waiver of liability with the Building Division, and permits under Chapter 1307 still apply.

A hired contractor must hold the registration first, and one who starts without it pays double the fee. Ask any contractor for the city registration before work begins.

sections.h2: How the Trumbull County Board of Revision works
sections.html:
Three county offices, the Auditor, the Treasurer and the Commissioners, or their representatives, make up the board. It rules on value complaints and on denied homestead or owner-occupancy claims, and it leaves the tax dollars on your bill alone. Whoever files carries the burden of proof.

  • Complaints go to the Auditor's office, which acts as the board's secretary. Email goes to BOR@co.trumbull.oh.us. A handwritten form needs a notary, and a typed form sent by email does not.
  • Useful evidence includes appraisals, photos, repair estimates and a recent settlement statement and purchase agreement.
  • Notice of a hearing arrives at least ten days ahead, and you may attend in person, by phone or on video.

The filing window under Ohio Revised Code 5715.19 closes at the end of March following the tax year. An outside party can seek a higher value only when a recent arm's length sale beat the listed value by ten percent and by a state threshold, set at $567,000 for tax year 2025.

The Warren City School District runs four preK to 8 schools and Warren G. Harding High School. Declining population led to a redistricting plan, a new Harding building and the demolition of several early 20th century elementary and junior high schools, so a buyer comparing school buildings should ask the district which one serves a given street.

Downtown still centers on the Trumbull County Courthouse, built beginning in 1895, along with a Carnegie Law Library and bank and office buildings from the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

Many Warren sales start with an estate. Under Ohio Revised Code 5302.30, an heir who hasn't lived in the house during the past year is excused from the state disclosure form, and so is a fiduciary selling for an estate, guardianship or trust. Other sellers of one-to-four unit homes must hand over the signed form.

Even then, buyers ask about known defects, so answer in writing and keep a copy.

A freeway carrying Ohio 82 bypasses the city, and Ohio 5 leads southwest to the Ohio Turnpike. US 422 and Ohio 45 also run through Warren. The city sees about 27.9 inches of snow per year on 21 snowy days, and January lows average 16.8 degrees. Plan showings around plowed walks, working heat and visible roof and gutter condition, since buyers check these first in winter.

sections.h2: A short checklist before you list
sections.html:
Warren sellers can save time by sorting the city items first. If the house is a rental, confirm the dwelling permit and tell the buyer it won't transfer. If you've moved out and plan to sell without a broker, register the vacant property or secure it so the fee can be avoided. If you plan repairs, check whether the contractor is registered, or file the owner waiver if you're doing the work yourself.

Then turn to the county. Decide whether the value complaint window is still open, and whether any homestead or owner-occupancy claim needs attention before closing. A cash buyer who takes the house as-is won't ask for a repair list, but the permit, registry and disclosure rules still apply to the sale, so it pays to have them straight before the first offer arrives.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to sell a rental house in Warren?
faqs.a: The dwelling permit in section 1367.10 does not transfer when the house sells. The buyer applies for a new one, and the Water Department wants proof of it before opening service.

faqs.q: What if I move out and list the house myself?
faqs.a: An empty house offered for sale by its owner counts as vacant under Chapter 1338 and must be registered within 30 days. A broker-listed house gets a six-month pass from the start of the listing.

faqs.q: When is the deadline to dispute my property value in Trumbull County?
faqs.a: By the end of March after the tax year, or the first-half collection date when that is later. Call the Auditor at 330-675-2420 for the current dates.

faqs.q: Does an inherited house need the Ohio disclosure form?
faqs.a: Usually not. Section 5302.30 excuses an heir who hasn't lived in the house for a year and also excuses fiduciaries acting for an estate.

faqs.q: Can I keep my homestead exemption after I sell?
faqs.a: No. The exemption belongs to the home you own and live in on January 1, so it ends with the sale. Your next home needs its own application with the county auditor.
